_note: Conventions the TypeScript scanner reads: how a route is declared, how it is guarded, how routers are mounted, how the web calls the API, what a table reference looks like, which table names carry sensitive data, what an admin URL looks like, and the MODULES - the business areas files belong to (first matching rule wins; narrow product areas first, broad platform buckets last). A project overrides any field in <project>/.cockpit/plugins/architecture.typescript.json with the same shape; `modules` there REPLACES this list. Regexes are strings; flags as given.

route._why: three shapes: app.get('/x') (Hono/Express), route('GET', '/x') and a module's ['GET', '/x', handler] rows (the node-app starter). A route path always begins with / - without that anchor c.get("orgId") made 1,398 'routes'. Named groups so the alternatives line up (Node 24 allows the same name per alternative).

call._why: the generic between the name and the paren: api<T>("/api/v1/...") - without it 23 calls were found in 1,398 files instead of 558

authNote: no requirePermission on the route; the API still applies requireAuth, so any signed-in role reaches it

modules._why: the node-app starter: a module is a unit - modules\<name>\ is the feature. keyFrom = the capture group that names it. A project with its own areas replaces this list (e.g. 17 business areas by path regex).
